memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Afterward, Joshua read all the words of the law — the blessings and the curses — just as it is written in the Book of the Law. There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read to the whole assembly of Israel, including the women and children, and the foreigners who lived among them. — Josh 8:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua reads the entire law to the whole assembly — the blessings and the curses, every single word. Nothing is left out. And notice carefully who is included: "the whole assembly of Israel, including the women and children, and the foreigners who lived among them." Everyone hears God's word. Men and women, young and old, native and foreigner alike. God's word is for all His people, not a privileged few.

There is a precious lesson here about the value of Scripture. Joshua did not pick and choose the pleasant parts. He read the blessings and the curses, the comforting words and the challenging ones. God's people need the whole counsel of God, not just the portions we find easy. We are tempted to underline only the encouraging verses and skip past the hard warnings. But we grow healthy only when we receive all of God's word, both its promises and its warnings.

Notice too that children were included. God's word was not held back from the young. From the earliest age, they were meant to hear and know the Scriptures. This is a beautiful pattern for families and churches: bring the young into the hearing of God's word, for it is able to make them "wise for salvation" (2 Tim 3:15).

Above all, this scene reminds us how central Scripture is to the life of God's people. We are a people formed and fed by God's word. And all of that word — its blessings and its warnings, its law and its promises — finds its fulfilment and its "yes" in Christ (2 Cor 1:20). To treasure the whole of Scripture is, in the end, to be led again and again to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you embrace the whole of God's word, or only the comfortable parts?
2. Are you helping children and young ones hear and know the Scriptures?
3. How does it deepen your love for Scripture to know all of it points to Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me a love for the whole of Your word — its promises and its warnings alike. Help me treasure Scripture and share it with the young, for it all points me to Christ. Amen.
